title: Work and Experience
grammarNote: The present perfect (he trabajado, ¿alguna vez has...?, todavía no he...) links past experience to the present moment, while the preterite is reserved for a specific, dated event. This lesson also sustains formal 'usted' register throughout and introduces 'hace + tiempo + que' to mark how long ago something started.

phrases.target: He trabajado en marketing durante cinco años
phrases.native: I have worked in marketing for five years
phrases.phonetic: eh trah-bah-HAH-doh en MAR-keh-teeng doo-RAN-teh SEEN-koh AH-nyos
phrases.vocabularyIntro: The present perfect 'he trabajado' connects a span of past work directly to the present — you're still building on that experience now.

exampleSentence.target: He trabajado en marketing durante cinco años en total.
exampleSentence.native: I have worked in marketing for five years in total.

phrases.grammarNote: Present perfect ('he trabajado') describes an ongoing or cumulative experience relevant to now, unlike the preterite, which would pin the work to a closed, dated period.
phrases.memoryHook: 'He' + past participle is your 'accumulated experience so far' marker — like a running tally.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I have worked in marketing for five years
practiceItems.answer: He trabajado en marketing durante cinco años

practiceItems.prompt: He ___ en marketing durante cinco años.

phrases.target: ¿Alguna vez ha liderado un equipo grande?
phrases.native: Have you ever led a large team?
phrases.phonetic: al-GOO-nah ves ah lee-deh-RAH-doh oon eh-KEE-poh GRAN-deh
phrases.vocabularyIntro: '¿Alguna vez ha...?' (Have you ever...?) is the standard present-perfect question for probing lifetime experience in a formal interview.

exampleSentence.target: ¿Alguna vez ha liderado un equipo grande en su puesto anterior?
exampleSentence.native: Have you ever led a large team in your previous position?

phrases.grammarNote: 'Ha liderado' uses formal 'usted' conjugation of the present perfect, appropriate throughout this interview register.
phrases.memoryHook: 'Alguna vez' (ever, at some point) is the built-in trigger word for present perfect questions.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Have you ever led a large team?
practiceItems.answer: ¿Alguna vez ha liderado un equipo grande?

practiceItems.prompt: ¿Qué le preguntan sobre liderar equipos en una entrevista?
practiceItems.answer: Alguna vez ha liderado un equipo grande

phrases.target: El año pasado lideré un proyecto muy grande
phrases.native: Last year I led a very big project
phrases.phonetic: el AH-nyoh pah-SAH-doh lee-deh-REH oon proh-YEK-toh MOO-ee GRAN-deh
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Lideré' is preterite — used here to give a concrete, dated example that answers the general present-perfect question with specifics.

exampleSentence.target: El año pasado lideré un proyecto muy grande para un cliente internacional.
exampleSentence.native: Last year I led a very big project for an international client.

phrases.grammarNote: Once you've claimed general experience with the present perfect ('he liderado equipos'), switch to the preterite ('lideré') to cite one specific, closed instance — this is the key usage boundary of the lesson.
phrases.memoryHook: 'El año pasado' (last year) anchors the action to one dated point, pulling you out of the perfect and into the preterite.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Last year I led a very big project
practiceItems.answer: El año pasado lideré un proyecto muy grande

practiceItems.prompt: El año pasado ___ un proyecto muy grande.

phrases.target: Todavía no he trabajado en una empresa internacional
phrases.native: I haven't worked at an international company yet
phrases.phonetic: toh-dah-VEE-ah noh eh trah-bah-HAH-doh en OO-nah em-PREH-sah een-ter-nah-see-oh-NAL
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Todavía no he...' (I haven't ... yet) marks a gap in experience up to this present moment, leaving the door open for the future.

exampleSentence.target: Todavía no he trabajado en una empresa internacional, pero me interesa mucho.
exampleSentence.native: I haven't worked at an international company yet, but it interests me a lot.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Todavía no he + participio' keeps the experience gap open-ended, contrasting with a preterite negative like 'no trabajé', which would close it to one specific occasion.
phrases.memoryHook: 'Todavía' (still/yet) plus negative present perfect signals 'the door is still open for this to happen'.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I haven't worked at an international company yet
practiceItems.answer: Todavía no he trabajado en una empresa internacional

practiceItems.prompt: Todavía no he trabajado en una empresa ___.

practiceItems.answer: Todavía no he trabajado en una empresa internacional
